key_insight: ActMOF turns real microwave MOF synthesis data into a benchmark for testing active-learning strategies, showing that Gaussian-process-based policies work especially well in sparse crystallization search spaces.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps engineers choose and compare optimization methods before running costly experiments, improving the efficiency of reticular synthesis development.
method: Emulated experimental MOF crystallization conditions from measured microwave syntheses.
Assigned each condition a crystallinity index from diffraction peak intensity and peak width.
Benchmarked Gaussian processes, tree ensembles, and LLM-guided search policies for active learning.
evidence_signal: Using a fixed budget of 12 experiments per campaign, the benchmark found GP-family policies among the strongest performers and successfully transferred guidance to six related aluminum MOF syntheses, all yielding crystalline products.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and representativeness of sparse experimental data, so benchmark results may not transfer uniformly across other MOF families or synthesis platforms.
paper_title: ActMOF: Mapping Reticular Synthesis through Active Learning
